problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate drone inspections across eight remote sensor stations:

Station Alpha: Position (85,188)
Station Beta: Position (175,39)
Station Gamma: Position (42,160)
Station Delta: Position (144,96)
Station Epsilon: Position (163,22)
Station Zeta: Position (16,21)
Station Eta: Position (50,191)
Station Theta: Position (56,15)

The flight distances between stations, in kilometers, are precisely known:
Alpha to Gamma: 51.3 km
Alpha to Delta: 109.3 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 183.4 km
Alpha to Zeta: 180.7 km
Alpha to Eta: 35.1 km
Alpha to Theta: 175.4 km
Beta to Gamma: 179.8 km
Beta to Delta: 64.9 km
Beta to Epsilon: 20.8 km
Beta to Zeta: 160.0 km
Beta to Eta: 196.8 km
Beta to Theta: 121.4 km
Gamma to Delta: 120.4 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 183.5 km
Gamma to Zeta: 141.4 km
Gamma to Eta: 32.0 km
Gamma to Theta: 145.7 km
Delta to Epsilon: 76.4 km
Delta to Zeta: 148.4 km
Delta to Eta: 133.6 km
Delta to Theta: 119.6 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 147.0 km
Epsilon to Eta: 203.3 km
Epsilon to Theta: 107.2 km
Zeta to Eta: 173.4 km
Zeta to Theta: 40.4 km
Eta to Theta: 176.1 km

Due to a permanent signal interference zone, direct flight between Station Alpha and Station Beta is impossible. Furthermore, operational protocols mandate that exactly one of two critical flight corridors must be utilized: either the link between Station Beta and Station Gamma, or the link between Station Gamma and Station Delta.

The objective is to determine the most fuel-efficient inspection circuit, where the drone must visit every station exactly once before returning to its origin, thereby minimizing the total flight distance.
